commitResults.messageTitle: Add date prefix and attendance date parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
AttendanceDate exists, but command parsers have no shared date prefix or conversion helper. The attendance parser needs both to accept a date consistently with other person attributes.

Add the date prefix and parse helper with validation and whitespace trimming. Cover valid, invalid, and null inputs so later command parsing can rely on the same behavior.

Attendance requests need a command representation before recording is added in v1.3.

Add a command that holds the displayed index and optional date, returns a clear placeholder result, and leaves the model untouched. Keep the date optional so the default date can be decided in v1.3.

The attendance command has a date conversion helper, but no parser turns command arguments into an attendance request.

Add parsing for a required displayed index and optional date. Reject malformed indices, invalid dates, and duplicate date prefixes with the existing parser error conventions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add command to mark a whole class present
commitResults.messageBody:
Attendance is marked one student at a time, making a full tutorial
slow to record. Issue #109 asks for a whole-class operation.

Add a command that marks every enrolled student and skips existing
records so repeated requests are safe. Reuse the single-student
helper while leaving that command unchanged.

Attendance requests containing only a class are rejected as missing
a student, preventing whole-class marking through the CLI.

Route requests with a class but no index or matriculation number to
the whole-class command and list the form in attendance usage text.
Preserve single-student parsing and its error precedence.

The guides describe only individual attendance marking, leaving
the whole-class form undocumented.

Document its syntax, skip behaviour, execution and manual checks
so tutors and maintainers can use and verify the feature.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify that unmarking does not store absences
commitResults.messageBody:
The UG tells tutors to "record absentees" by marking a whole class
and unmarking absent students. Unmarking deletes the attendance
record, so TAssist ends up with no record rather than an absence.

The wording implies an absence status is saved, which contradicts
the DG glossary's statement that no record does not mean absence.

Reword the bullet to describe the workflow as taking attendance
quickly, and state that unmarking removes only that class and date's
record and that absences are not stored.

commitResults.messageTitle: Persist assignment marks with student data
commitResults.messageBody:
Save shared definitions and student entries in JSON so marks survive
restart. Keep unmarked entries distinct from recorded zero marks.

Load older files with an empty gradebook. Reject invalid definitions,
references, duplicates, and scores during restoration so corrupt data
does not replace the saved records.

Create shared assignment definitions and attach them to a student in one
command. Allow a shorter form to attach an existing definition without
repeating its name or maximum mark.

Resolve students by matriculation number across the stored list and
reject duplicate definitions or links without changing records.
Document this command while mark entry and display follow later.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark command for assigned work
commitResults.messageBody:
Record numeric scores for a student's existing assignment and allow
later entries to replace the previous score. Report whether a score was
first recorded or updated, keeping zero distinct from an unmarked entry.

Validate the student, assignment, link, and maximum before changing data.
Document the command and verify that saved marks survive reopening.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show assignment results with marks command
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors can record marks but cannot inspect all results for an
assignment in one place. Display the shared definition and every
assigned student with a score or explicit unmarked status.

Read from the gradebook and stored students, sort by matriculation
number, and leave the current student filter unchanged.
Allow tutors to remove one student's assignment or remove a shared assignment and all its marks. Preserve student records and unrelated results. Document both forms and verify their saved state.

Short scientific-notation values can expand into enormous decimal
strings during display and JSON saving. Limit their plain form to
64 characters to keep the app responsive and avoid excessive memory
use. Apply the same validation to saved data.

Update both guides and cover the new behavior with command tests.

for an empty history, and remove it when the sort is reset. Update the
guides and cover ordering and display state with tests.

commitResults.messageBody:
# Conflicts:

Tutors need to compare results for one assignment without mixing marks
from different assessments. Add an assignment-specific sort with
recorded marks first and explicit missing states on student cards.

Reset a mark sort when underlying student or gradebook data changes
so the displayed comparison remains accurate. Document the command and
cover parsing, ordering, missing values, and error handling.

The sort parser treats keyword case inconsistently and reports a generic usage message for malformed assignment IDs. Review comments also identify unclear method names and an incomplete command summary.

Accept case-insensitive sort keywords and report assignment ID constraints. Rename the display and parser helpers, clarify the command summary, and keep UI details in the implementation guide.
